bugs.headline: Pubd Memory Leak Due to Telemetry Failing from Expired "sdn-network-infra-iwan" Certificate
bugs.description:
Symptom: A device may experience a memory leak in the "pubd" process when telemetry fails due to a DNAC certificate expiring, In the below example, this process is the top user of RSS memory. 
Router#show processes memory platform sorted 
System memory: 7748420K total, 7444384K used, 304036K free,
Lowest: 234596K
   Pid    Text      Data   Stack   Dynamic       RSS              Name  
----------------------------------------------------------------------
 12371      91   3911928     136   3828692   3911928              pubd
Conditions: Telemetry is failing, and it's due to the DNAC cert having expired as seen in the "end" value under the "validity date": 
Router# show telemetry connection all
Telemetry connections
Index Peer Address               Port  VRF Source Address             State      State Description
----- -------------------------- ----- --- -------------------------- ---------- --------------------
39726 x.x.x.x       xxxx 0   x.x.x.x               Connecting Connection request made to transport handler >> Connection failing.

Router#show crypto pki certificates sdn-network-infra-iwan 
Certificate
  Status: Available
  Certificate Serial Number (hex): XXXXX
  Certificate Usage: General Purpose
  Issuer: 
    cn=sdn-network-infra-ca
  Subject:
    Name: XXXXX
    cn=XXXXX_sdn-network-infra-iwan
    hostname=XXXXX
  Validity Date: 
    start date: 09:30:28 UTC Aug 22 2022
    end   date: 09:30:28 UTC Aug 22 2023 <===
  Associated Trustpoints: sdn-network-infra-iwan 
  Storage: nvram:sdn-network-#XXX.cer
Workaround: Fix the DNAC certificate by using "force configuration push" per: https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/cloud-systems-management/network-automation-and-management/catalyst-center/2-3-7/user_guide/b_cisco_catalyst_center_user_guide_237/b_cisco_dna_center_ug_2_3_7_chapter_01010.html Bug CSCwk39268 may also contribute to the automatic renewal failing in the first place. To clear memory that has already been consumed under pubd, run "no netconf-yang" from config mode, wait 15 seconds, and then re-enter "netconf-yang". Further Problem Description: None. PSIRT Evaluation: The Cisco PSIRT has evaluated this issue and determined it does not meet the criteria for PSIRT ownership or involvement. This issue will be addressed via normal resolution channels. If you believe that there is new information that would cause a change in the severity of this issue, please contact psirt@cisco.com for another evaluation. Additional information on Cisco's security vulnerability policy can be found at the following URL: http://www.cisco.com/en/US/products/products_security_vulnerability_policy.html

bugs.headline: Grpc tx thread stuck issue leading to ble_transport memory leak
bugs.description: AP Crash Symptom: Grpc tx thread of ble_transport gets stuck leading to high memory usage and resulting in updates not getting sent to Spaces Conditions: when the grpc connection between ap and connector flacky and keeps flapping Workaround: AP reload Further Problem Description: due to tx thread of the ble_transport being stuck, ble_transport is not able to drain the packets form the tx queue. this results in queue build up leading to high memory usage. This high memory usage by ble_transport may impacket other functionality of wireless on ap due to low memory available.

bugs.headline: ASA/FTD: Memory leak observed on ASA 9.22.2.14
bugs.description: Symptom: FPR-3130 running ASA version 9.22(2)14, the ASA/LINA exhibits gradual memory utilization increase over several weeks, despite no changes in traffic volume or configuration. The issue appears to be related to memory optimization behavior by the aggregateAuthDataHandler. Memory usage eventually exceeds 90%, at which point the system requires a reload to recover. Conditions: * SSL VPN/ * First seen while using Multiple Certificate Authentication. Workaround: Reloading temporarily resolves the issue. Further Problem Description: N/A
